extracted.intended_audience: patent lawyers, litigators, judges, and law students studying U.S. patent litigation procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing how defendants must plead and give notice of particular defenses in U.S. patent infringement actions (distinguishing general issue, special pleas, and the specific facts/defenses that require pre-trial notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: General issue sufficient for defenses denying cause of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The general issue is a sufficient plea for all defenses which deny the existence of a cause of action in the plaintiff (i.e., any defence which puts in issue any averment of the declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes defenses contesting patentability, patentee's right to the monopoly, existence or validity of the patent, title of the plaintiff, or defendant's practice without authority. The general issue may be used with or without notice where statute requires notice for certain defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute of Limitations requires special plea
rubrics_metrics.description: The defence of the Statute of Limitations recognizes a subsisting cause of action but avers plaintiff's laches; this defence requires a special plea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike the other defences that deny the cause of action, limitations must be specially pleaded at common law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special pleas when tendering specific issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant may plead specially any or all defenses (except denial of performance of the infringing act) when he desires to tender a specific issue to be traversed by the plaintiff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a special plea sets up facts of which statutory notice is required, the plea must not only be filed as a plea but must be served on the plaintiff in the mode provided by statute; the same matter may not be presented both in a special plea and by a notice under the general issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice required when pleading general issue to prove certain facts
rubrics_metrics.description: When the defendant pleads the general issue he must give written notice to the plaintiff if he desires to offer evidence tending to prove any one of five specified states of fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a rule of evidence intended to protect the plaintiff from surprise; the statute enumerates the particular categories that require notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraudulent specification (notice required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice required where the defence rests on the allegation that the specification filed by the patentee was made to contain less than the whole truth or more than is necessary (i.e., was intended to deceive the public).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A merely insufficient specification (as opposed to fraudulent) is not within this state of facts and may be urged under the general issue without notice. The fraudulent specification is treated as the 'eleventh' defence in statutory lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreptitious or unjust procurement (notice required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice required where defendant alleges the patentee surreptitiously or unjustly obtained the patent for what was in fact invented by another who was using reasonable diligence in adapting and perfecting the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clause addresses cases of wrongful appropriation by a later patentee of another's invention in the course of that other's diligent reduction to practice; it is distinct from mere prior invention/anticipation and was intended to warn of this special inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication or prior patent (notice required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice required where the defence rests on the allegation that the invention had been patented or described in some printed publication prior to the patentee's supposed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under later statutes (e.g., act of 1870) prior patent was explicitly added; a prior publication cannot be offered to prove want of novelty unless notice has been given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not original/first inventor or prior use (notice required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice required where defendant claims the patentee was not the original and first inventor/discoverer of a material and substantial part of the thing patented (this embraces prior use, prior knowledge, and related claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is broad and intended to cover all alleged prior use/knowledge in the U.S. before the patentee's alleged inventive act; statutes evolved to include prior use concepts and the disclosure of names/residences of those alleged to have used/knew the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use or sale >2 years / abandonment to the public (notice required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice required where the defence rests on the allegation that the invention had been in public use or on sale in the U.S. for more than two years before application or had been abandoned to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier acts varied on this point; later acts extended the requirement to all forms of abandonment. Upon due notice the defendant may show two years' public use and sale prior to application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement is a rule of evidence to prevent surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory rule requiring notice when certain defenses are to be presented is a rule of evidence, not of pleading; it protects the plaintiff against surprise and does not change the burden of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule has been and must be varied over time as justice demands, but such variations don't alter parties' burdens or court posture except for the duty to give prescribed notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special plea must possess notice attributes to substitute for statutory notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A special plea may be substituted for the statutory notice only if the plea possesses the necessary attributes of the notice as to completeness of statement and time and mode of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A special plea that adequately performs the function of notice (i.e., serves as fair warning) is legitimate; otherwise the statutory mode of notice is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment (scope and notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment to the public includes acts giving conclusive presumption of intent to surrender the invention and broader patterns of conduct manifesting the same; notice is required when pleading abandonment as a defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier statutes sometimes required no notice for abandonment; later acts (e.g., 1870 onward) made notice essential whenever abandonment is urged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior invention vs. imitation distinctions for notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory language and decisions distinguish between prior rival inventors (who may have used/reduced to practice) and mere imitators; notice clauses were crafted to give warning appropriate to these differing inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the defence is that a patentee was anticipated by prior reduction to practice, the inquiry focuses on conception and diligence; different statutory clauses were meant to signal different kinds of challenges and to avoid misleading the patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — inventive_skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the alleged invention is not the product of inventive skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the ordinary defences that may be pleaded and proved under the general issue without giving statutory notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — protected_classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That it does not fall within either of the protected classes of inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be presented under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That it is not useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be presented under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — nonexistence_of_patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That no such patent as the one declared upon has ever existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be presented under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — issued_contrary_to_law
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the plaintiff's patent was issued contrary to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be presented under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — nature_of_invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the invention described in the patent is neither an art, a machine, a manufacture, a composition of matter, a design, nor an improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be presented under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — ambiguous_specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the specification is ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ambiguity in the specification may be urged under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — excessive_claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the claim is excessive and has not been cured within reasonable time by a disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be presented under the general issue without notice; relates to overbroad claims and corrective disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — ambiguous_claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the claim is ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim ambiguity is a defense that can be raised under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — surrender_of_patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the patent in force at the date of the infringement has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent was surrendered before the alleged infringement, that fact may be shown under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — repeal_of_patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the patent declared on has been repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously repealed patents are a matter for proof under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — lack_of_title_to_sue
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the plaintiff has no such title to the patent as enables him to sue at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues of standing or title to bring suit may be raised under the general issue without statutory notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — nonidentity_of_invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the invention practised by the defendant is not identical with the one covered by the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-infringement (nonidentity) is among the defenses that can be presented under the general issue without notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences admissible under the general issue without notice — nature_of_defendant_acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Defence: That the acts of the defendant in reference to the patented invention were not acts (continuation cut off in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text continues beyond the chunk; this entry captures the visible fragment indicating that certain characterizations of the defendant's acts (e.g., whether they constitute infringement or not) are provable under the general issue without notice.
